title: Making Money — The Complete Wealth Creation Engine
purpose: A practical, evidence-led educational system connecting income, ownership, investing, business, legal tax planning, risk control and compounding.
disclaimer: Educational information only. It is not personalised investment, financial, legal or tax advice. Investments can fall in value and users may lose capital. Tax outcomes depend on jurisdiction and individual circumstances.

pathways.title: Starting From Zero
pathways.focus: Earn first, stop leakage, stabilise cash flow and build the first emergency buffer.
steps: List essential monthly costs and all expensive debt.
Choose one saleable service that can be offered within seven days.
Complete a 14-day skill sprint using free resources.
Contact ten potential customers or employers each working day.
Direct the first surplus to a small emergency reserve before speculation.
Begin a tiny automated investment only after essential bills and expensive debt are controlled.

pathways.title: Building Momentum
pathways.focus: Automate saving, increase earning power, own diversified productive assets and test a small business.
steps: Set a target savings rate that is realistic and repeatable.
Use tax-efficient accounts available in the selected jurisdiction.
Keep investment fees and turnover low.
Build a second income stream around an existing skill or local need.
Review progress quarterly and rebalance annually.

pathways.title: Compounding Wealth
pathways.focus: Diversify concentration, improve structures, control tax leakage and protect downside.
steps: Map all assets, liabilities, ownership and beneficiaries.
Separate operating risk from long-term assets where legally appropriate.
Use a written investment policy and concentration limits.
Review company, pension, insurance, estate and succession structures with qualified advisers.

pathways.title: Protecting Established Wealth
pathways.focus: Governance, succession, asset protection, tax compliance and intergenerational planning.
steps: Create a family balance sheet and ownership map.
Document decision rights, liquidity needs and succession.
Use regulated legal, tax and investment professionals.
Avoid structures whose only justification is secrecy or an implausible tax result.

zeroMoneySprint.title: The First 30 Days With No Money

weeks.title: Stop the bleeding
actions: Cancel or renegotiate non-essential recurring costs.
List debt by interest rate and minimum payment.
Protect rent, food, energy, transport and essential insurance first.

weeks.title: Create an offer
actions: Choose a service based on a skill, local problem or existing equipment.
Write a one-sentence offer with price and result.
Ask real people what they would pay for before building anything.

weeks.title: Sell before scaling
actions: Contact 50 potential buyers, employers or partners.
Deliver one small paid job well.
Collect proof, a testimonial and a referral.

weeks.title: Build repeatability
actions: Raise price only after evidence of demand.
Set aside tax and operating costs immediately.

weeks.title: Create the first asset
actions: Pay down the most expensive debt.
Create a recurring offer, reusable product or automated saving rule.

capitalFlows.why: Private AI investment and hyperscale capital expenditure are expanding quickly.
capitalFlows.accessible: Broad technology, semiconductor, infrastructure and power-system research rather than chasing one headline stock.
capitalFlows.risks: Valuation, power constraints, rapid obsolescence and market concentration.

capitalFlows.why: Power demand and new generation are outgrowing grid capacity in many regions.
capitalFlows.accessible: Regulated utilities, diversified infrastructure funds, equipment supply chains and skills.
capitalFlows.risks: Regulation, permitting, debt costs and project delays.

capitalFlows.sector: Energy security, nuclear and domestic supply
capitalFlows.why: Security concerns are redirecting capital toward resilient domestic energy systems.
capitalFlows.accessible: Diversified energy and infrastructure research; specialist exposure requires high risk tolerance.
capitalFlows.risks: Policy reversals, cost overruns, commodity cycles and geopolitics.

capitalFlows.why: More digital systems, AI use and critical infrastructure create a larger attack surface.
capitalFlows.accessible: Skills, services, diversified funds and profitable operators with recurring revenue.
capitalFlows.risks: Crowded valuations, product obsolescence and customer concentration.
capitalFlows.source: Public company filings and regulator threat reports

capitalFlows.why: Labour constraints and AI capability are accelerating investment in physical automation.
capitalFlows.accessible: Industrial suppliers, software, sensors, logistics and specialist skills.
capitalFlows.risks: Long sales cycles, capital intensity and unreliable forecasts.

capitalFlows.sector: Water, climate adaptation and resilient infrastructure
capitalFlows.why: Aging systems, extreme weather and population growth create non-discretionary investment needs.
capitalFlows.accessible: Utilities, engineering, equipment, infrastructure funds and local service businesses.
capitalFlows.risks: Political pricing, slow procurement and project execution.

capitalFlows.why: Ageing populations and scientific tools support long-term demand.
capitalFlows.accessible: Diversified healthcare exposure and skills rather than binary clinical bets.
capitalFlows.risks: Regulation, reimbursement, patent expiry and trial failure.

capitalFlows.why: Security spending and supply-chain redesign are increasing procurement and domestic capacity.
capitalFlows.accessible: Public contractors, industrial suppliers and specialist employment.
capitalFlows.risks: Political change, ethical constraints, procurement cycles and valuation.

copyRich.why: Fortunes usually come from equity, not wages alone.
copyRich.accessible: Build a small business, own diversified shares or create intellectual property.

copyRich.strategy: Concentrate to create, diversify to preserve
copyRich.why: A focused company can create wealth; later diversification limits ruin.
copyRich.accessible: Focus career or business effort while keeping personal reserves diversified.

copyRich.strategy: Use legal entities for a purpose
copyRich.why: Companies and holding structures can separate operations, ownership and succession.
copyRich.accessible: Use the simplest structure justified by liability, tax and administration.
copyRich.risk: Cost, reporting failures and aggressive tax schemes.

copyRich.why: Qualified advice can prevent expensive legal, tax and investment mistakes.
copyRich.accessible: Pay for focused annual advice instead of building a family office.

copyRich.why: Small annual leakage compounds against the owner.
copyRich.accessible: Low-cost products, correct account wrappers and lawful deductions.
copyRich.risk: Letting tax reduction override investment quality.

copyRich.why: Cash prevents forced sales and creates optionality.
copyRich.accessible: Emergency reserves and planned sinking funds.
copyRich.risk: Holding excessive idle cash for long periods.

structures.name: Sole trader / individual business
structures.use: Simple trading and early-stage service income.
structures.warning: Personal liability and tax treatment vary by jurisdiction.

structures.name: Limited company
structures.use: Separate legal personality, contracts, payroll and retained profits.
structures.when: Growing trading activity, liability or partners justify administration.

structures.name: Holding company
structures.use: Own operating subsidiaries or long-term investments separately.
structures.when: Multiple businesses, sale proceeds or reinvestment strategy justify it.
structures.warning: Professional legal and tax design is essential.

structures.name: Property company / SPV
structures.use: Hold a defined property or project.
structures.when: Lenders, partners or liability separation require it.
structures.warning: Financing, tax and extraction costs can outweigh benefits.

structures.name: Trust
structures.use: Hold assets under legal duties for beneficiaries in jurisdictions that recognise trusts.
structures.when: Succession, vulnerable beneficiaries or complex family governance.
structures.warning: Trusts are jurisdiction-specific, costly and heavily reportable; they are not secrecy devices.

structures.name: Foundation
structures.use: Pursue charitable or family-governance purposes under relevant law.
structures.when: Substantial assets and a defined long-term purpose.
structures.warning: Not a universal substitute for a trust or company.

structures.name: Pension / retirement wrapper
structures.use: Long-term retirement saving with jurisdiction-specific tax treatment.
structures.when: Eligible earned income and long time horizon.
structures.warning: Access restrictions, fees and future tax rules matter.

structures.name: Family investment company
structures.use: Pool and govern family investments through corporate ownership.
structures.when: Substantial family capital and succession needs justify ongoing administration.
structures.warning: Requires specialist advice; gifts, control and tax consequences must be modelled.

franceTax.warning: France-specific figures are educational snapshots from official sources and must be rechecked before action.

items.title: Income-tax bands
items.detail: Official 2026 guidance lists rates of 0%, 11%, 30%, 41% and 45%, with thresholds applied per tax-share.

items.title: Micro-enterprise thresholds
items.detail: Official 2026 guidance sets new turnover ceilings, including €203,100 for qualifying sales and €83,600 for qualifying services, subject to activity-specific rules.

items.title: Micro regime and expenses
items.detail: The micro regime generally applies a fixed allowance rather than deducting actual professional expenses; a real regime may be worth examining where costs are high.

items.title: PEA and assurance-vie
items.detail: Both are long-term French investment wrappers with different access, asset and tax rules. Tax depends on holding period and transaction type.

items.title: Professional review
items.detail: Compare EI, micro, EURL, SARL, SASU and SAS based on liability, social contributions, cash extraction, VAT and administration—not one tax rate alone.

futureScenarios.theme: AI infrastructure becomes an electricity and construction story
futureScenarios.case: Capital may continue moving from model developers into chips, networking, cooling, data centres, grids and generation.
futureScenarios.risk: A spending boom can still produce poor investor returns if prices already assume perfection.
futureScenarios.evidence: Stanford AI Index 2026; IMF 2026 AI investment analysis.

futureScenarios.theme: The grid becomes a global bottleneck
futureScenarios.case: Electricity networks, transformers, storage and demand management may receive sustained investment because generation and large loads are connecting faster than grids can expand.
futureScenarios.risk: Regulated returns, political pricing and construction delays.

futureScenarios.case: Countries may finance a wider mix of nuclear, renewables, storage, gas infrastructure, efficiency and domestic supply to reduce strategic vulnerability.

futureScenarios.theme: Automation spreads from software into physical work
futureScenarios.case: Robotics, sensors and agentic software may reshape logistics, manufacturing, healthcare administration and field services.
futureScenarios.risk: Demonstrations may not translate into reliable commercial margins.

futureScenarios.theme: Human trust and verification become paid infrastructure
futureScenarios.case: As synthetic content expands, identity, provenance, cybersecurity, auditing and trusted expert services may gain value.
futureScenarios.evidence: Analytical scenario based on expanding digital systems.

futureScenarios.theme: Skills with direct revenue or physical-world value outperform generic knowledge work
futureScenarios.case: Sales, skilled trades, healthcare, cybersecurity, engineering, operations and AI-enabled entrepreneurship may remain defensible because they combine judgment, trust or physical execution.
futureScenarios.evidence: Scenario; verify against national labour data.
